move: cursor clicks Next, step slides left; clicks Back, slides home
how: An onboarding card shows four progress dashes, a step viewport and a grey Back and blue Next button. Cursor enters with power3.out in the first 15% of the 4s loop and hovers Next: an overlay fades in, the button lifts 3px and scales 1.03, its arrow nudges 5px right. Press at 0.8s (20%) scales 0.95 with power2.in for 0.1s, release rebounds to 1.03 with back.out(3). At 0.9s step 1 slides out with xPercent -110 and step 2 slides in from 110% with expo.inOut over 0.55s while the second progress dash fills with scaleX 0 to 1 power3.out and Back brightens from 0.45 to full opacity. The cursor then travels to Back (power3.inOut, 0.7s), repeats the hover/press at 2.2 to 2.67s, the steps slide back and the dash empties from the right, Back dims, and the cursor exits by 3.9s so the first frame returns.
adapt: Replace the step copy, dash count, button labels and the blue accent; the cursor target coordinates nx/ny are computed from the card layout constants and must be recomputed if the card size changes. Keep expo.inOut 0.55s slides and the back.out(3) release.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the card with dots, two steps, two buttons and a cursor inside el. animate returns the timeline with the same sequence at fractions of D (Next press 0.2D, slide 0.225D, Back press 0.64D, return slide 0.66D, exit 0.825D). Scope all selectors to el and derive nx/ny from the card element's layout rather than hard-coded numbers.
caveats: cursor positions are hard-coded from card layout math
only two of four steps exist; dashes 3 and 4 never fill
